body:
## Problem

`merge._wait_for_green` now re-reads the rollup one poll interval after the first green (#582, PR #617), but it compares only the overall verdict, not which checks are present. A slow job that hasn't registered within one poll interval (15 s) still gets through:

- `green(dco)` → `green(dco)` merges on a partial rollup.
- `green(dco)` → `green(dco, e2e)` "confirms" on a different set of checks.

PR #617 states this itself ("this narrows #582 but does not fully close it", `pr-description.md`), and the advisory code review said the issue should not be counted as fully fixed. The docstring at `template/src/pdca_harness/merge.py:157-159` (PR branch `fix/582-merge-wait-confirms-green`) records the gap.

## Done when

A merge under `merge_requires = "all"` needs evidence that the rollup is complete, not only green twice. For example, the confirm read compares check names/counts with the first read, or the operator can configure a list of expected checks. A test pins `green(dco)` → `green(dco)` (with `e2e` registering later) as refused.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_582 PR body + advisory code review). Residual of #582.
title: merge: the confirm read compares only the verdict, so a slow check that registers after 15 s still merges on a partial rollup (residual of #582)
